extracted.intended_audience: literary scholars, critics, and creative writers studying narrative theory (graduate-level)
extracted.subtask_description: Analyzing or producing fiction using James Phelan's rhetorical theory of narrative, emphasizing how narrative functions as rhetoric, how textual and reader dynamics synthesize into progression, and how characters and narration are evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative is rhetoric
rubrics_metrics.description: "Someone telling someone else, on some occasion and for some purpose, that something happened."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat narrative as a communicative act with a teller, an audience, an occasion, and a purpose; analyze how rhetorical choices (what to tell, how, and why) shape meaning and reader response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading is multidimensional
rubrics_metrics.description: Reading simultaneously engages intellect, emotion, ideology, and ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess a work across multiple response modes rather than solely cognitive interpretation—attend to emotional effects, ideological implications, and ethical positioning as integral evaluative dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Progression (synthesis of textual + reader dynamics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Progression = the synthesis of textual dynamics + reader dynamics; a narrative moves forward by introducing instabilities/tensions, complicating them, and resolving (or refusing to resolve) them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how well the text creates and develops instabilities/tensions and how the reader's judgments evolve; coherence of movement (introduce → complicate → resolve/refuse) is central to narrative success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textual Dynamics — Instabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Instabilities: tensions among characters in the storyworld.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the strength, clarity, and productive complication of interpersonal or plot-based tensions in the storyworld; weak or underdeveloped instabilities yield flat narrative motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textual Dynamics — Tensions (narrational)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tensions: tensions among the implied author, narrator, and audience (i.e., differences in knowledge, value, perception).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze mismatches in perspective, information, and values between narrator/implied author and implied audience; these tensions generate narrational interest and shape reader judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader Dynamics — Interpretive judgments
rubrics_metrics.description: Reader makes interpretive judgments about what is happening in the narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track how the text prompts readers to form, revise, or hold interpretations; strong narratives manage and exploit interpretive work rather than leaving it inert or incoherent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader Dynamics — Ethical judgments
rubrics_metrics.description: Reader makes ethical judgments about characters' actions and the narrator's reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine how the narrative invites readers to judge characters and narrators morally, whether it guides, manipulates, or opens space for resistance, and whether ethical positioning is explicit or implicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader Dynamics — Aesthetic judgments
rubrics_metrics.description: Reader makes aesthetic judgments about the work's form and execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include assessments of craft, style, formal choices, and how these contribute to or detract from narrative aims; consider whether aesthetic effects align with rhetorical purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Synthesizing Move
rubrics_metrics.description: "The progression of instability is accompanied by narrative judgments." Reading is the simultaneous tracking of textual dynamics and the formation of judgments about them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the interaction between textual events (instabilities/tensions) and the reader's evolving judgments; strength lies in productive interplay rather than isolated textual action or passive reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character Component — Mimetic
rubrics_metrics.description: Mimetic — the character as person (psychology, plausibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess characters for believable psychology and plausible behavior within the storyworld; lack of mimetic credibility can undermine reader engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character Component — Thematic
rubrics_metrics.description: Thematic — the character as representative of an idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how characters function as embodiments of themes or ideas; excessive thematic dominance can make characters allegorical or didactic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character Component — Synthetic
rubrics_metrics.description: Synthetic — the character as artifact (constructed for the work's purpose).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend to how characters are crafted as rhetorical/poetic constructions serving narrative aims; evaluate how constructional choices advance the work's purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of Mimetic, Thematic, and Synthetic functions
rubrics_metrics.description: A successful work integrates all three; imbalance produces flatness or didacticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether mimetic plausibility, thematic force, and synthetic construction are balanced; note when overemphasis on one dimension (e.g., purely thematic) weakens character complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unreliable Narration — Misreporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Misreporting (a form of unreliability): narrator reports events inaccurately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagnose instances where the narrator's factual reports contradict other narrative evidence; evaluate how misreporting affects reader interpretation and ethical/aesthetic response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unreliable Narration — Misreading
rubrics_metrics.description: Misreading (misinterpreting): narrator misinterprets events or motives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify when a narrator's interpretive accounts are shown to be mistaken by textual evidence; consider how this shapes irony, dramatic tension, or thematic complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unreliable Narration — Misregarding
rubrics_metrics.description: Misregarding (mis-evaluating ethically): narrator evaluates characters' actions or values incorrectly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate ethical misjudgments made by narrators and their rhetorical consequences—whether they prompt reader correction, critique, or complicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unreliable Narration — Underreporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Underreporting: narrator omits relevant factual information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for gaps or silences in narration that withhold facts; assess whether omissions are strategic (to create suspense or irony) or negligent (confusing or manipulative).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unreliable Narration — Underreading
rubrics_metrics.description: Underreading: narrator fails to interpret or perceive fully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spot limited perceptual or interpretive frames that cause narrators to miss significance; consider how underreading shapes reader sympathy or critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unreliable Narration — Underregarding
rubrics_metrics.description: Underregarding: narrator fails to evaluate ethically what is significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze ethical blind spots or minimizations by the narrator and their effect on the reader's ethical work; determine whether the text invites correction or complicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Position of Narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Every narrative situates the reader in an ethical position — by inviting certain judgments about characters and asking the reader to share, resist, or revise them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the honesty and clarity of the work's ethical stance: does it transparently invite certain judgments, manipulate readers covertly, or open productive ethical ambiguities? Ethical criticism is obligatory for any reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit Evaluative Criteria (summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: A narrative can be analyzed on: strength of instabilities (in storyworld); strength of tensions (in narration); coherence of progression (introduce → complicate → resolve); integration of mimetic/thematic/synthetic character functions; honesty of the ethical position the work implies; specificity of any unreliable narration (which type?).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these explicit dimensions as a checklist when evaluating a narrative; quantify or describe each dimension's strength and interrelation to give a rounded critical judgment.
